plan: [My value is $4. I want to avoid overbidding in Stage 1. Bidding my value in Stage 1 means I exit at clock price $4. If the other two bidders have values greater than $4, they will continue bidding until one of them exits. If one of them has a value less than $4, I will win at a price equal to the second highest bid. If both of them have values less than $4, I will win at a price equal to the highest bid. I will bid my value. ]

[My value is $23. In the ascending clock auction, I want to stay in as long as the clock price is below my value. Therefore, I want my exit price (sealed bid) to be equal to my value. This way, I guarantee that I will stay in until the clock reaches my value. If the other bidders have lower values, I win. If they have higher values, I lose, but that's okay because I wouldn't want to pay more than my value anyway. Therefore, my sealed bid should be my value.]

[I will bid a fraction of my value in stage 1. A good starting point is 0.8 times my value. This will allow me to stay in the auction longer if the other bids are low, and exit gracefully if they are high. This allows me to potentially win with a profit if the second highest bid is lower than my value. If I bid too low, I might miss out on potential profit. If I bid too high, I might end up overpaying. I will adjust the fraction in future rounds based on the results.]
